adds.title: Country Policy and Information Note: sexual orientation, gender identity and expression and sex characteristics – Nigeria, June 2025 (GOV.UK)
adds.summary: The UK government's June 2025 country-policy note on Nigeria records the framework a visitor to Adamawa stands under: same-sex sexual acts between men are criminalised with up to 14 years' imprisonment under the secular Criminal Code, and the Same Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act makes entering a same-sex marriage or civil union punishable by 14 years' imprisonment, with 10 years for anyone who 'administers, witnesses, abets or aides the solemnization' of one or supports the registration and operation of gay clubs and organisations. It further states that sharia penal codes apply to Muslims in the 12 northern states with death as the maximum penalty for men, that sharia courts have imposed at least four death sentences since 2022 (none carried out), and that NGOs document tens of LGBT+ arrests per year while police and Islamic police subject LGBT+ people to beatings, blackmail, extortion and torture. This is the allied-government national-framework source underpinning the record's federal-penalty and northern-climate claims for Adamawa; the note's 12-sharia-states list does not name Adamawa.

adds.title: LGBT rights in Nigeria – Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's Nigeria article is the national-framework source the record relies on: the Same-Sex Marriage Prohibition Act 2013, signed into law in January 2014, makes same-sex marriage or civil union 'invalid and illegal', carries up to 14 years' imprisonment for entering one, and criminalises those who register, operate or participate in gay clubs, societies and organisations or make public show of same-sex amorous relationships; in 2022 a federal court ruled sections of the Act unconstitutional and unenforceable. The article names the 12 northern sharia-law states (Bauchi, Borno, Gombe, Jigawa, Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Kebbi, Niger, Sokoto, Yobe and Zamfara) where the death penalty applies to men — a list that does not include Adamawa, corroborating the record's statement that the sources do not name Adamawa as a sharia state while the federal 14-year framework and nationwide arrest climate apply.

adds.title: Country Policy and Information Note: sexual orientation, gender identity and expression and sex characteristics – Nigeria, June 2025 (GOV.UK)
adds.summary: The UK government's June 2025 country-policy note records the framework a visitor to Abia stands under: same-sex sexual acts between men carry up to 14 years' imprisonment under secular law, and the Same Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act makes entering a same-sex marriage or civil union punishable by 14 years' imprisonment while giving 10 years to anyone who 'administers, witnesses, abets or aides the solemnization' of one or supports the registration, operation and sustenance of gay clubs, societies, organisations, processions or meetings. The note states that sharia penal codes apply to Muslims in the 12 northern states (death as the maximum penalty for men, with at least four sharia death sentences imposed since 2022 and none carried out) and documents tens of LGBT+ arrests per year plus police and Islamic-police harassment including beatings, blackmail, extortion and torture. The note does not reach Abia as a sharia state, matching the record's statement that the northern sharia provisions do not reach this southern state while federal penalties and the national arrest climate apply in full.

adds.title: LGBT rights in Nigeria – Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's Nigeria article is the national-framework source for Abia: the Same-Sex Marriage Prohibition Act 2013, in force from January 2014, criminalises same-sex unions with up to 14 years' imprisonment and also punishes registering, operating or participating in gay clubs, societies and organisations and public displays of same-sex amorous relationships, with a 2022 federal court ruling striking down sections of the Act as unconstitutional. It lists the 12 northern states operating sharia criminal law for Muslims (Bauchi, Borno, Gombe, Jigawa, Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Kebbi, Niger, Sokoto, Yobe and Zamfara) — Abia is not among them, corroborating the record's claim that the sharia provisions do not reach this southern state while the federal 14-year framework and the national climate of arrests and community hostility apply.
